title: Socket API minimalism and tool-call compression — PRD draft
summary: Lightweight socket API design focused on reducing client integration friction and per-request overhead for incremental streaming + tool call workflows. Primary idea: a tiny deterministic frame set + optional compression for tool payload bodies so mobile and low-bandwidth clients get predictable latency and small tail p99. Emphasis on SDK ergonomics to hide frame/codec complexity.
goals: 1) Define a minimal wire protocol (<= 8 frame types) that supports: incremental text frames, typed tool-call frames (call / result / error), flow-control, and short binary blobs for attachments. 2) Add an optional per-request compression layer (two codecs: gzip and a small bespoke delta codec) to reduce token/body sizes for mobile. 3) Provide concrete SDK surface recommendations so client teams can adopt with minimal changes. 4) Target p50 end-to-end incremental-first latency <= 40ms for edge clients (US region) and p99 network budget <= 250ms for small requests (< 1KB pre-compression).
non_goals: 1) Replacing existing REST/HTTP endpoints. 2) Designing an all-new authentication model — will reuse existing token + tenant headers. 3) Building language-specific SDKs in this doc (this is API + ergonomics; implementation PRDs live elsewhere).
user_personas: - Mobile app frontend engineer (needs small binary and fast connect). - Server-side orchestration service (wants efficient fanout and batching). - Third-party integration partner (limited control over network, wants a simple socket example).
primary_user_flows: 1) Connect: client opens socket, performs minimal handshake, subscribes to session id. 2) Request: client sends 'invoke' frame with prompt metadata; runtime may stream incremental 'token' frames and then send either 'tool_call' frame or final 'done' frame. 3) Tool call: runtime emits 'tool_call' frame containing tool_id + arguments (optionally compressed); client or local proxy executes tool and returns 'tool_result' frame. 4) Resume/reconnect: client provides last-acked frame id to resume partial stream.
wire_format: - Frame header: 1 byte type | 3 bytes length (big-endian) | 4 bytes monotonic frame id (uint32). - Frame types (proposed, 8 total): 0x01 CONNECT_ACK, 0x02 INVOKE, 0x03 TOKEN_CHUNK, 0x04 TOOL_CALL, 0x05 TOOL_RESULT, 0x06 ERROR, 0x07 PING/PONG, 0x08 DONE. - Payload: raw UTF-8 for small text frames; binary for attachments. - Compression flag: highest bit of type byte signals payload compressed. Supported algorithms: 0x01 gzip, 0x02 delta-x (simple run-length delta for small JSON diffs). - Schema: tool frames must include JSON header (short) with keys: tid, seq, opt_compress, checksum. Header intentionally tiny (< 256 bytes) to keep parse fast.
example_sequence: Client -> CONNECT; Server -> CONNECT_ACK(session=abc123). Client -> INVOKE(prompt_meta). Server -> TOKEN_CHUNK('The quick '), TOKEN_CHUNK('brown fox'), TOOL_CALL(tool_id=web_search, args={q:'brown fox habitat'}, compressed=1). Client/proxy -> TOOL_RESULT(tool_id=web_search, result={...}, compressed=1). Server -> TOKEN_CHUNK(' found an article'), DONE. Client -> ACK final_frame_id.
sdk_ergonomics: - Provide a minimal higher-level SDK method: socketClient.invoke(options) -> returns an async iterator of events (token, tool_call, done, error). - The SDK hides compression: SDK chooses whether to compress args by heuristics (body_size > 512 bytes OR repeated sessions). - Provide one-line migration: replace http.invoke() with socketClient.invokeStream() returning same logical messages. - Backoff/connect policy: automatic exponential reconnect with binary resume id; transparent to developer (configurable). - Small helper: built-in tool-call handler shim that routes TOOL_CALL frames to a local callback or to an http webhook, selectable by developer via registration: registerToolHandler(tool_id, handlerFn).
observability_and_telemetry: - Emit frame-level telemetry: frames_sent, frames_recv, per-frame-latency histogram, compression_savings (bytes_before/after). - Token-chunk size histogram and tool-call roundtrip latency. - Track resume_success_rate and resume_gap_size. - Suggest server-side logs for tool_call routing decisions and fallback occurrences. - Default sampling: 1% of flows for full payload capture; rate-limited on heavy clients.
security_and_compatibility: - Reuse existing Bearer token header in initial handshake. - Frame-level checksums to detect corruption (CRC32). - Compression disabled for frames marked 'sensitive' via header flag. - Version byte in handshake to allow graceful negotiation and server-side backward compatibility. - No plaintext storage of tool args on disk unless policy flags allow on tenant side.
performance_targets: - Cold connect time (TLS + handshake) p50 <= 80ms, p95 <= 220ms (US regions). - Per-token streaming overhead <= 8ms added by framing/parse on typical mobile CPU. - Compression heuristics should reduce median body bytes by >= 40% for web-search-style tool args. - Resume success rate >= 99.7% under intermittent networks (simulated 15% packet loss).
rollout_phases: - Phase 0 (lab): implement protocol and test harness, run local sims with packet loss and reconnections (2 sprints). - Phase 1 (alpha): SDK + server side opt-in for 5 internal apps; collect telemetry and fix edge cases (1 month). - Phase 2 (beta): expose to partners and selected external customers behind feature flag; provide migration guide. - Phase 3 (GA): enable for all tenants with backward compatibility and documentation. - Post-GA: iterate on codec choices and consider adding brotli and a compiled delta codec if telemetry supports it.
success_metrics: - Adoption: 30% of new streaming integrations using socket API within 6 months of GA. - Latency: 10% reduction in p99 end-to-end latency for mobile clients using streaming flows. - Cost: 15% reduction in bandwidth bill for customers using compression for tool calls. - Stability: resume_success_rate >= 99.7% and disconnect-induced failures < 0.5% of streaming sessions.
open_questions: Should we add a multiplexing substream id to support multiple logical conversations in one TCP socket? (tradeoff: header size vs multiplex benefits)
Which languages should get first-class SDKs at beta (JS/TS, Python, Swift, Kotlin)?
Is delta-x codec IP we can ship as open-source, or do we need a patent review?
compatibility_notes: - Servers must accept both compressed and uncompressed frames. - If a client connects with an older version, server must fall back to plain text frames and log a deprecation metric. - Define a migration window of 6 months for older SDKs before warning signals escalate in console.
developer_docs_plan: - Quickstart: 10-minute tutorial showing socket connect + invoke + tool handler in JS. - API reference: Frame type table, header fields, compression flags. - Troubleshooting: common resume failures and how to debug. - Migration guide: HTTP -> socket sample patterns and cost/latency tradeoffs.
next_steps: 1) Engineering spike: implement a prototype server + JS SDK shim (2 weeks). 2) Run mobile device benchmarks with 3 network profiles (wifi, 4G, 3G). 3) Design sample telemetry dashboard tiles and add resume/fragment charts to Console. 4) Prepare alpha rollout checklist and internal docs.
notes_to_self: Keep header as small as possible. Re-evaluate compression threshold after initial telemetry. Consider a 'no-serialization' path for edge proxies that want raw token frames only.
editorial_style: informal working doc: concise bullets, examples, and explicit open questions. Expect many follow-ups and a small set of breaking design decisions around multiplexing and codec choice.
